Subject: Performance SLO qualification — latency & throughput follow-up

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap of the perf/SLO items we discussed and next steps for an initial POC: 

1) Target SLOs you described
   - p95 generation latency: 200 ms for median payloads (see payloads below)
   - Steady-state throughput: 300 req/s across peak region
   - Peak concurrency: ~50 concurrent streaming sessions
   - Streaming: required (partial tokens need to be delivered as they’re produced)

2) Payload profile (from call) — please confirm with sample traffic:
   - Typical user prompt: ~60–100 tokens (avg ~80)
   - Typical model response: ~100–140 tokens (avg ~120)
   - 60% of requests are repeatable prefixes (high cache hit potential)

3) Cost / perf levers we recommended (high level)
   - Continuous batching: combine short requests into micro-batches to improve GPU utilization while keeping tail latency bounded
   - KV/prefix caching: 30s–60s TTL for repeated prefixes to avoid recomputing early tokens
   - Quantization profiles: test 4-bit quantized variant for large inferencing cost savings; fall back to fp16 for high-quality edge cases
   - Model variants: consider a smaller cheaper model for short/low-risk responses and larger model for high-quality outputs with automatic routing

4) Suggested POC scope / metrics
   - 1-hour load validation at 300 req/s to validate p95 latency and streaming behavior
   - Measure cost per 1M tokens under candidate configs (quantized vs fp16, batching strategies)
   - Latency breakdown: network + queuing + generation p95/p99

Attachments: I’ve attached our latest mutual action plan (avery-mup-v2.pdf) and a quick SLO calc spreadsheet (slo-calc.xlsx). If you can share a sanitized 1-hour traffic sample (headers + token sizes) that’ll speed up sizing.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
   - Sarah/Tom: share sanitized traffic sample and confirm whether 200 ms p95 is firm or a stretch target (action: Sarah)
   - Redwood: provide an initial config recommendation and a rough cost delta for quantized vs fp16 (action: Marissa / Nikhil)
   - Schedule POC load window (30–60min): target week of Mar 16th — open to earlier if you can share sample traffic this week

Thanks — short follow-up meeting works well once we have the traffic sample.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- 200 ms p95 is our goal, but we can tolerate 350 ms p95 during business hours for the first 60 days of the POC.
- Confirming payload averages: our telemetry shows avg prompt ~80 tokens, avg response ~120 tokens — matches your notes.
- Streaming is mandatory; we need partial responses as they’re produced for our UI (progressive rendering).
- 60% prefix reuse is an approximation — we will include a sample export showing session IDs + prompt lengths.

I attached a sanitized traffic sample (traffic-sample-20260305.json) — contains timestamps, token counts, and a flag for streaming sessions. Please treat as PII-free sample.

Also would like a ballpark cost estimate: how much difference do you expect between 4-bit quantized vs fp16 for our workload? A per-1M-token delta would be ideal.

Happy to schedule the POC window; Mar 16th works for us but we can be flexible.

—Sarah

Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification — latency & throughput follow-up

Looping in some quick sizing / recommendations based on the sample Sarah sent and the target SLOs. High level: feasible with tuned config and a small dedicated footprint; main risks are streaming tail latency and cacheability variance.

Prelim observations from traffic-sample-20260305.json:
 - Avg request tokens: 82; avg response tokens: 118
 - Peak observed rps in sample: 280 (10-minute spike), sustained ~210 rps
 - 58% sessions show repeated prefixes within 45s windows (cache hit candidate)

Initial config to try in POC:
 - Model: redwood-llama-13b-quant4 (primary) with redwood-llama-13b-fp16 as backup for low-latency critical flows
 - Serving: reserved dedicated pool (2–4 cards depending on final perf) to avoid noisy neighbors — helps guarantee p95 SLAs
 - Batching: continuous batching with dynamic max_batch=64 and a batching latency cap of 15 ms to avoid excessive queueing
 - KV/prefix caching: enable prefix cache with 30s TTL and local hot-cache on GPU serving nodes
 - Streaming: use token-level streaming hooks with backpressure window set to 16 tokens to reduce jitter at the network layer

Rough cost delta estimate (very preliminary) based on model runtime estimates and token sizes:
 - fp16 baseline: X (we'll compute exact)
 - quant4: ~35–45% lower inference cost per token vs fp16 for this workload (ballpark)

Questions / asks before we schedule the load window:
 - Confirm whether fallback routing is acceptable (i.e., route to fp16 for flagged high-quality sessions)
 - Can Avery provide a 1-hour continuous sample at ~300 rps (or permission to replay current sample at that rate)?
 - Any regulatory constraints (data residency / no-export) that would require Private deployment vs Dedicated?

I can produce a short runbook and a tuned tuning matrix for the POC once we agree on the replay window.

-Nikhil
